106	  async findByISBN(isbn: string): Promise<OpenLibraryIsbnLookupResult> {
107	    var book = await this.openLibrary.isbnLookup(isbn) as OpenLibraryIsbnLookupResult
108	    if (book.errorCode) {
109	      Logger.error('Book not found')
110	    }
111	    return book
112	  }
113	
114	  filterSearchResults(books: OpenLibraryBookResult[], title: string, author: string | null | undefined, maxTitleDistance: number, maxAuthorDistance: number): OpenLibraryBookResult[] {
115	    var searchTitle = cleanTitleForCompares(title)
116	    var searchAuthor = cleanAuthorForCompares(author)
117	    return books
118	      .map((b) => {
119	        b.cleanedTitle = cleanTitleForCompares(b.title)
120	        b.titleDistance = levenshteinDistance(b.cleanedTitle, title)
121	
122	        // Total length of search (title or both title & author)
123	        b.totalPossibleDistance = b.title.length
124	
125	        if (author) {
126	          if (!b.author) {
127	            b.authorDistance = author.length
128	          } else {
129	            b.totalPossibleDistance += b.author.length
130	            b.cleanedAuthor = cleanAuthorForCompares(b.author)
131	
132	            var cleanedAuthorDistance = levenshteinDistance(b.cleanedAuthor, searchAuthor)
133	            var authorDistance = levenshteinDistance(b.author || '', author)
134	
135	            // Use best distance
136	            b.authorDistance = Math.min(cleanedAuthorDistance, authorDistance)
137	
138	            // Check book author contains searchAuthor
139	            if (searchAuthor.length > 4 && b.cleanedAuthor.includes(searchAuthor)) b.includesAuthor = searchAuthor
140	            else if (author.length > 4 && b.author.includes(author)) b.includesAuthor = author
141	          }
142	        }
143	        b.totalDistance = b.titleDistance + (b.authorDistance || 0)
144	
145	        // Check book title contains the searchTitle
146	        if (searchTitle.length > 4 && b.cleanedTitle.includes(searchTitle)) b.includesTitle = searchTitle
147	        else if (title.length > 4 && b.title.includes(title)) b.includesTitle = title
148	
149	        return b
150	      })
151	      .filter((b) => {
152	        if (b.includesTitle) {
153	          // If search title was found in result title then skip over leven distance check
154	          if (this.verbose) Logger.debug(`Exact title was included in "${b.title}", Search: "${b.includesTitle}"`)
155	        } else if (Number(b.titleDistance) > maxTitleDistance) {
156	          if (this.verbose) Logger.debug(`Filtering out search result title distance = ${b.titleDistance}: "${b.cleanedTitle}"/"${searchTitle}"`)
157	          return false
158	        }
159	
160	        if (author) {
161	          if (b.includesAuthor) {
162	            // If search author was found in result author then skip over leven distance check
163	            if (this.verbose) Logger.debug(`Exact author was included in "${b.author}", Search: "${b.includesAuthor}"`)
164	          } else if (Number(b.authorDistance) > maxAuthorDistance) {
165	            if (this.verbose) Logger.debug(`Filtering out search result "${b.author}", author distance = ${b.authorDistance}: "${b.author}"/"${author}"`)
166	            return false
167	          }
168	        }
169	
170	        // If book total search length < 5 and was not exact match, then filter out
171	        if (Number(b.totalPossibleDistance) < 5 && Number(b.totalDistance) > 0) return false
172	        return true
173	      })
174	  }

179	   * @param {string} author
180	   * @param {number} maxTitleDistance
181	   * @param {number} maxAuthorDistance
182	   * @returns {Promise<Object[]>}
183	   */

class AudioTrack {
  constructor() {
    this.index = null
    this.startOffset = null
    this.duration = null
    this.title = null
    this.contentUrl = null
    this.mimeType = null
    this.codec = null
    this.metadata = null
  }

  toJSON() {
    return {
      index: this.index,
      startOffset: this.startOffset,
      duration: this.duration,
      title: this.title,
      contentUrl: this.contentUrl,
      mimeType: this.mimeType,
      codec: this.codec,
      metadata: this.metadata?.toJSON() || null
    }
  }

  setData(itemId, audioFile, startOffset) {
    this.index = audioFile.index
    this.startOffset = startOffset
    this.duration = audioFile.duration
    this.title = audioFile.metadata.filename || ''

    this.contentUrl = `/api/items/${itemId}/file/${audioFile.ino}`
    this.mimeType = audioFile.mimeType
    this.codec = audioFile.codec || null
    this.metadata = audioFile.metadata.clone()
  }

  setFromStream(title, duration, contentUrl) {
    this.index = 1
    this.startOffset = 0
    this.duration = duration
    this.title = title
    this.contentUrl = contentUrl
    this.mimeType = 'application/vnd.apple.mpegurl'
  }
}
module.exports = AudioTrack

1	function parseNfoMetadata(nfoText) {
2	  if (!nfoText) return null
3	  const lines = nfoText.split(/\r?\n/)
4	  const metadata = {}
5	  let insideBookDescription = false
6	  lines.forEach(line => {
7	    if (line.search(/^\s*book description\s*$/i) !== -1) {
8	      insideBookDescription = true
9	      return
10	    }
11	    if (insideBookDescription) {
12	      if (line.search(/^\s*=+\s*$/i) !== -1) return
13	      metadata.description = metadata.description || ''
14	      metadata.description += line + '\n'
15	      return
16	    }
17	    const match = line.match(/^(.*?):(.*)$/)
18	    if (match) {
19	      const key = match[1].toLowerCase().trim()
20	      const value = match[2].trim()
21	      if (!value) return
22	      switch (key) {
23	        case 'title':
24	          {
25	            const titleMatch = value.match(/^(.*?): (.*)$/)
26	            if (titleMatch) {
27	              metadata.title = titleMatch[1].trim()
28	              metadata.subtitle = titleMatch[2].trim()
29	            } else {
30	              metadata.title = value
31	            }
32	          }
33	          break
34	        case 'author':
35	          metadata.authors = value.split(/\s*,\s*/).filter(v => v)
36	          break
37	        case 'narrator':
38	        case 'read by':
39	          metadata.narrators = value.split(/\s*,\s*/).filter(v => v)
40	          break
41	        case 'series name':
42	          metadata.series = value
43	          break
44	        case 'genre':
45	          metadata.genres = value.split(/\s*,\s*/).filter(v => v)
46	          break
47	        case 'tags':
48	          metadata.tags = value.split(/\s*,\s*/).filter(v => v)
49	          break
50	        case 'copyright':
51	        case 'audible.com release':
52	        case 'audiobook copyright':
53	        case 'book copyright':
54	        case 'recording copyright':
55	        case 'release date':
56	        case 'date':
57	          {
58	            const year = extractYear(value)
59	            if (year) {
60	              metadata.publishedYear = year
61	            }
62	          }
63	          break
64	        case 'position in series':
65	          metadata.sequence = value
66	          break
67	        case 'unabridged':
68	          metadata.abridged = value.toLowerCase() === 'yes' ? false : true
69	          break
70	        case 'abridged':
71	          metadata.abridged = value.toLowerCase() === 'no' ? false : true
72	          break
73	        case 'publisher':
74	          metadata.publisher = value
75	          break
76	        case 'asin':
77	          metadata.asin = value
78	          break
79	        case 'isbn':
80	        case 'isbn-10':
81	        case 'isbn-13':
82	          metadata.isbn = value
83	          break
84	        case 'language':
85	        case 'lang':
86	          metadata.language = value
87	          break
88	      }
89	    }
90	  })

93	  if (metadata.description) {
94	    metadata.description = metadata.description.trim()
95	  }
96

98	}

const optionDefinitions = [
  { name: 'config', alias: 'c', type: String },
  { name: 'metadata', alias: 'm', type: String },
  { name: 'port', alias: 'p', type: String },
  { name: 'host', alias: 'h', type: String },
  { name: 'source', alias: 's', type: String },
  { name: 'dev', alias: 'd', type: Boolean },
  // Run in production mode and use dev.js config
  { name: 'prod-with-dev-env', alias: 'r', type: Boolean }
]

const commandLineArgs = require('./server/libs/commandLineArgs')
const options = commandLineArgs(optionDefinitions)

const Path = require('path')
process.env.NODE_ENV = options.dev ? 'development' : process.env.NODE_ENV || 'production'

const server = require('./server/Server')
global.appRoot = Path.basename(__dirname) === 'dist-server' ? Path.resolve(__dirname, '..') : __dirname

const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'
if (isDev || options['prod-with-dev-env']) {
  const devEnv = require('./dev').config
  if (devEnv.Port) process.env.PORT = devEnv.Port
  if (devEnv.ConfigPath) process.env.CONFIG_PATH = devEnv.ConfigPath
  if (devEnv.MetadataPath) process.env.METADATA_PATH = devEnv.MetadataPath
  if (devEnv.FFmpegPath) process.env.FFMPEG_PATH = devEnv.FFmpegPath
  if (devEnv.FFProbePath) process.env.FFPROBE_PATH = devEnv.FFProbePath
  if (devEnv.NunicodePath) process.env.NUSQLITE3_PATH = devEnv.NunicodePath
  if (devEnv.SkipBinariesCheck) process.env.SKIP_BINARIES_CHECK = '1'
  if (devEnv.AllowIframe) process.env.ALLOW_IFRAME = '1'
  if (devEnv.BackupPath) process.env.BACKUP_PATH = devEnv.BackupPath
  if (devEnv.ReactClientPath) process.env.REACT_CLIENT_PATH = devEnv.ReactClientPath
  if (devEnv.AllowedDevOrigins) {
    process.env.ALLOWED_DEV_ORIGINS = Array.isArray(devEnv.AllowedDevOrigins) ? devEnv.AllowedDevOrigins.join(',') : String(devEnv.AllowedDevOrigins)
  }
  process.env.SOURCE = 'local'
  process.env.ROUTER_BASE_PATH = devEnv.RouterBasePath ?? '/audiobookshelf'
}

const inputConfig = options.config ? Path.resolve(options.config) : null
const inputMetadata = options.metadata ? Path.resolve(options.metadata) : null

const PORT = options.port || process.env.PORT || 3333
const HOST = options.host || process.env.HOST
const CONFIG_PATH = inputConfig || process.env.CONFIG_PATH || Path.resolve('config')
const METADATA_PATH = inputMetadata || process.env.METADATA_PATH || Path.resolve('metadata')
const SOURCE = options.source || process.env.SOURCE || 'debian'

const ROUTER_BASE_PATH = process.env.ROUTER_BASE_PATH ?? '/audiobookshelf'

console.log(`Running in ${process.env.NODE_ENV} mode.`)
console.log(`Options: CONFIG_PATH=${CONFIG_PATH}, METADATA_PATH=${METADATA_PATH}, PORT=${PORT}, HOST=${HOST}, SOURCE=${SOURCE}, ROUTER_BASE_PATH=${ROUTER_BASE_PATH}`)

const Server = new server(SOURCE, PORT, HOST, CONFIG_PATH, METADATA_PATH, ROUTER_BASE_PATH)
Server.start()

ARG NUSQLITE3_DIR="/usr/local/lib/nusqlite3"
ARG NUSQLITE3_PATH="${NUSQLITE3_DIR}/libnusqlite3.so"

### STAGE 0: Build client ###
FROM node:24-alpine AS build-client

WORKDIR /client
COPY /client /client
RUN npm ci && npm cache clean --force
RUN npm run generate

### STAGE 1: Compile server on the builder CPU (avoid QEMU SIGILL from tsc on arm64) ###
FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM node:24-alpine AS compile-server

WORKDIR /server
COPY index.js package* tsconfig.server.json /server
COPY /server /server/server
RUN npm ci --include=dev --ignore-scripts && npm run build:server

### STAGE 2: Install native server deps for the target arch ###
FROM node:24-alpine AS build-server

ARG NUSQLITE3_DIR
ARG TARGETPLATFORM

ENV NODE_ENV=production

RUN apk add --no-cache --update \
  curl \
  make \
  python3 \
  g++ \
  unzip

WORKDIR /server
COPY index.js package* /server
COPY /server /server/server
COPY --from=compile-server /server/dist-server /server/dist-server

RUN case "$TARGETPLATFORM" in \
  "linux/amd64") \
  curl -L -o /tmp/library.zip "https://github.com/mikiher/nunicode-sqlite/releases/download/v1.2/libnusqlite3-linux-musl-x64.zip" ;; \
  "linux/arm64") \
  curl -L -o /tmp/library.zip "https://github.com/mikiher/nunicode-sqlite/releases/download/v1.2/libnusqlite3-linux-musl-arm64.zip" ;; \
  *) echo "Unsupported platform: $TARGETPLATFORM" && exit 1 ;; \
  esac && \
  unzip /tmp/library.zip -d $NUSQLITE3_DIR && \
  rm /tmp/library.zip

RUN npm ci --omit=dev

### STAGE 3: Create minimal runtime image ###
FROM node:24-alpine

ARG NUSQLITE3_DIR
ARG NUSQLITE3_PATH

# Install only runtime dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache --update \
  tzdata \
  ffmpeg \
  tini

WORKDIR /app

# Copy compiled frontend and server from build stages
COPY --from=build-client /client/dist /app/client/dist
COPY --from=build-server /server /app
COPY --from=build-server ${NUSQLITE3_PATH} ${NUSQLITE3_PATH}

EXPOSE 80

ENV PORT=80
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV CONFIG_PATH="/config"
ENV METADATA_PATH="/metadata"
ENV SOURCE="docker"
ENV NUSQLITE3_DIR=${NUSQLITE3_DIR}
ENV NUSQLITE3_PATH=${NUSQLITE3_PATH}

ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"]
CMD ["node", "dist-server/index.js"]

  python3 \
  g++ \
  unzip

WORKDIR /server
COPY index.js package* /server
COPY /server /server/server
COPY --from=compile-server /server/dist-server /server/dist-server

RUN case "$TARGETPLATFORM" in \
  "linux/amd64") \

  esac && \
  unzip /tmp/library.zip -d $NUSQLITE3_DIR && \
  rm /tmp/library.zip

RUN npm ci --omit=dev

### STAGE 3: Create minimal runtime image ###
FROM node:24-alpine

ARG NUSQLITE3_DIR
ARG NUSQLITE3_PATH

# Install only runtime dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache --update \
  tzdata \
  ffmpeg \
  tini

WORKDIR /app

# Copy compiled frontend and server from build stages
COPY --from=build-client /client/dist /app/client/dist
COPY --from=build-server /server /app
COPY --from=build-server ${NUSQLITE3_PATH} ${NUSQLITE3_PATH}

EXPOSE 80

ENV PORT=80
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV CONFIG_PATH="/config"
ENV METADATA_PATH="/metadata"
ENV SOURCE="docker"
ENV NUSQLITE3_DIR=${NUSQLITE3_DIR}
ENV NUSQLITE3_PATH=${NUSQLITE3_PATH}

ENTRYPOINT ["tini", "--"]
CMD ["node", "dist-server/index.js"]

=== .github/workflows/unit-tests.yml ===
name: Run Unit Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Branch/Tag/SHA to test'
        required: true
  pull_request:
  push:

jobs:
  run-unit-tests:
    name: Run Unit Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout (push/pull request)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch'

      - name: Checkout (workflow_dispatch)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Run tests
        run: npm test

=== .github/workflows/integration-test.yml ===
name: Integration Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches-ignore:
      - 'dependabot/**' # Don't run dependabot branches, as they are already covered by pull requests
    # Only build when files in these directories have been changed
    paths:
      - client/**
      - server/**
      - test/**
      - index.js
      - package.json
      - tsconfig.server.json

jobs:
  build:
    name: build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: setup node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: install pkg (using yao-pkg fork for targeting node24)
        run: npm install -g @yao-pkg/pkg

      - name: get client dependencies
        working-directory: client
        run: npm ci

      - name: build client
        working-directory: client
        run: npm run generate

      - name: get server dependencies and compile server
        run: npm ci && npm run build:server && npm prune --omit=dev

      - name: build binary
        run: pkg --config package.json -t node24-linux-x64 -o audiobookshelf dist-server/index.js

      - name: run audiobookshelf
        run: |
          ./audiobookshelf &
          sleep 5

      - name: test if server is available
        run: curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:3333 | grep Audiobookshelf

name: Run Component Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: 'Branch/Tag/SHA to test'
        required: true
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'client/**'
      - '.github/workflows/component-tests.yml'
  push:
    paths:
      - 'client/**'

jobs:
  run-component-tests:
    name: Run Component Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout (push/pull request)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Checkout (workflow_dispatch)
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
        if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          cd client
          npm ci

      - name: Run tests
        run: |
          cd client
          npm test

=== build/linuxpackager ===
#!/bin/bash
set -e
set -o pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" &> /dev/null && pwd )"

cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.."

# Get package version without double quotes
VERSION="$( eval echo $( jq '.version' package.json) )"
DESCRIPTION="$( eval echo $( jq '.description' package.json) )"
OUTPUT_FILE="audiobookshelf_${VERSION}_amd64.deb"

echo ">>> Building Client"
echo "--------------------"

cd client
rm -rf node_modules
npm ci
npm run generate
cd ..

echo ">>> Building Server"
echo "--------------------"

rm -rf node_modules
npm ci
npm run build:server

echo ">>> Packaging"
echo "--------------------"

# Create debian control file

mkdir -p dist
rm -rf dist/debian
cp -R build/debian dist/debian
chmod -R 775 dist/debian

controlfile="Package: audiobookshelf
Version: $VERSION
Section: base
Priority: optional
Architecture: amd64
Depends:
Maintainer: advplyr
Description: $DESCRIPTION"

echo "$controlfile" > dist/debian/DEBIAN/control;

# Package debian
pkg --config package.json -t node24-linux-x64 -o dist/debian/usr/share/audiobookshelf/audiobookshelf dist-server/index.js

fakeroot dpkg-deb -Zxz --build dist/debian

mv dist/debian.deb "dist/$OUTPUT_FILE"

echo "Finished! Filename: $OUTPUT_FILE"

=== TaskManager.js ===
const SocketAuthority = require('../SocketAuthority')
const Task = require('../objects/Task')

/**
 * @typedef TaskString
 * @property {string} text
 * @property {string} key
 * @property {string[]} [subs]
 */

class TaskManager {
  constructor() {
    /** @type {Task[]} */
    this.tasks = []
  }

  /**
   * Add task and emit socket task_started event
   *
   * @param {Task} task
   */
  addTask(task) {
    this.tasks.push(task)
    SocketAuthority.emitter('task_started', task.toJSON())
  }

  /**
   * Remove task and emit task_finished event
   *
   * @param {Task} task
   */
  taskFinished(task) {
    if (this.tasks.some((t) => t.id === task.id)) {
      this.tasks = this.tasks.filter((t) => t.id !== task.id)
      SocketAuthority.emitter('task_finished', task.toJSON())
    }
  }

  /**
   * Create new task and add
   *
   * @param {string} action
   * @param {TaskString} titleString
   * @param {TaskString|null} descriptionString
   * @param {boolean} showSuccess
   * @param {Object} [data]
   */
  createAndAddTask(action, titleString, descriptionString, showSuccess, data = {}) {
    const task = new Task()
    task.setData(action, titleString, descriptionString, showSuccess, data)
    this.addTask(task)
    return task
  }

  /**
   * Create new failed task and add
   *
   * @param {string} action
   * @param {TaskString} titleString
   * @param {TaskString|null} descriptionString
   * @param {TaskString} errorMessageString
   */
  createAndEmitFailedTask(action, titleString, descriptionString, errorMessageString) {
    const task = new Task()
    task.setData(action, titleString, descriptionString, false)
    task.setFailed(errorMessageString)
    SocketAuthority.emitter('task_started', task.toJSON())
    return task
  }
}
module.exports = new TaskManager()

class AudioTrack {
  constructor() {
    this.index = null
    this.startOffset = null
    this.duration = null
    this.title = null
    this.contentUrl = null
    this.mimeType = null
    this.codec = null
    this.metadata = null
  }

  toJSON() {
    return {
      index: this.index,
      startOffset: this.startOffset,
      duration: this.duration,
      title: this.title,
      contentUrl: this.contentUrl,
      mimeType: this.mimeType,
      codec: this.codec,

    }

    this.duration = audioFile.duration

    this.mimeType = audioFile.mimeType
    this.codec = audioFile.codec || null
    this.metadata = audioFile.metadata.clone()
  }

  setFromStream(title, duration, contentUrl) {
    this.index = 1
    this.startOffset = 0
    this.duration = duration
    this.title = title
    this.contentUrl = contentUrl
    this.mimeType = 'application/vnd.apple.mpegurl'
  }
}

#!/bin/bash
# Boots one compiled server tree in an isolated scratch directory, runs smoke.js against it, then stops it.
# Usage: runsmoke.sh <label> <path to compiled index.js> <port> <cwd for the server> [NODE_PATH]
# Nothing outside the scratchpad is written: config, metadata and the library all live under e2e/<label>.
SP="/c/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--SEM-2-574-po-s06-run-audiobookshelf/44babef5-5841-4659-9823-eee1f53febf0/scratchpad"
LABEL="$1"; INDEX="$2"; PORT="$3"; SERVER_CWD="$4"; NP="$5"
if [ -z "$LABEL" ] || [ -z "$INDEX" ] || [ -z "$PORT" ] || [ -z "$SERVER_CWD" ]; then echo "usage error"; exit 2; fi

RUN="$SP/e2e/$LABEL"
case "$RUN" in "$SP"/e2e/?*) ;; *) echo "refusing to use run dir $RUN"; exit 2 ;; esac
rm -rf "$RUN"
mkdir -p "$RUN/lib"
cp -r "$SP/smoke-src/." "$RUN/lib/"
RUNW="$(cygpath -m "$RUN")"

FFMPEG="$(cygpath -m "$(which ffmpeg)").exe"
FFPROBE="$(cygpath -m "$(which ffprobe)").exe"
[ -f "$FFMPEG" ] && [ -f "$FFPROBE" ] || { echo "ffmpeg/ffprobe not found"; exit 2; }

(
  cd "$SERVER_CWD" || exit 2
  # SKIP_BINARIES_CHECK stops the server from downloading ffmpeg; the two paths point at the copies already installed
  FFMPEG_PATH="$FFMPEG" FFPROBE_PATH="$FFPROBE" SKIP_BINARIES_CHECK=1 NODE_PATH="$NP" \
    node "$INDEX" --config "$RUNW/config" --metadata "$RUNW/metadata" --port "$PORT" --host 127.0.0.1 --source smoke > "$RUN/server.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$RUN/pid"
)
PID="$(cat "$RUN/pid")"

UP=0
for i in $(seq 1 80); do
  if curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/audiobookshelf/ping" > /dev/null 2>&1; then UP=1; break; fi
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 0.5
done
if [ "$UP" != 1 ]; then
  echo "[$LABEL] SERVER DID NOT COME UP"; tail -30 "$RUN/server.log"; kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 1
fi
echo "[$LABEL] server is up on 127.0.0.1:$PORT (pid $PID)"

node "$(cygpath -m "$SP/smoke.js")" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/audiobookshelf" "$RUNW/lib" "$RUNW/transcript.json"
SMOKE_EXIT=$?

kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.25; done
kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null
echo "[$LABEL] server stopped; smoke exit=$SMOKE_EXIT"
echo "[$LABEL] error/fatal lines in server log: $(grep -c -i -E "\b(ERROR|FATAL)\b" "$RUN/server.log")"
exit $SMOKE_EXIT

cd "D:/SEM-2/574/po-s06-run/audiobookshelf" && git add server/providers/OpenLibrary.ts && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
[PO-S06] OpenLibrary: type isbnLookup() by what the API returns

A live request showed that /isbn/<isbn> (no ".json" suffix) is answered
with the book's HTML page, so isbnLookup() resolves to that page as a
string, not to a JSON record as the previous annotation claimed. Widen the
return type to include string and note the quirk on the method.

The URL is left alone: correcting it would change behaviour, and the only
caller (BookFinder.findByISBN) is itself unused. Types and a comment only;
compiled code is unchanged and BookFinder.ts still compiles as is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git status --short | head -3; echo "(clean if nothing above)"

content.text:
All 14 files are now TypeScript, nothing was left unconverted, and the server behaves as before. The build passes, all 356 tests pass (the same list as before I started), and lint is clean.

The work is on branch `po-s06/typescript-migration` in 15 commits, each prefixed `[PO-S06]`. I branched because `master` was the only branch; it is still at `baseline`, so `git merge --ff-only po-s06/typescript-migration` brings it across.

## What I converted

Following `server/finders/`, I only added types and never edited runtime code. The middle column compares each file's compiled JavaScript with the build of the original `.js`.

| File | Compiled output vs. before | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `utils/globals` | byte-identical | lists typed read-only |
| `utils/longTimeout` | byte-identical | |
| `utils/stringifySequelizeQuery` | byte-identical | |
| `objects/files/AudioTrack` | byte-identical | |
| `objects/metadata/AudioMetaTags` | byte-identical | misspelt tag names are now build errors |
| `objects/Notification` | same program, comments differ | |
| `objects/Task` | same program, comments differ | |
| `objects/TrackProgressMonitor` | same program, comments differ | |
| `utils/areEquivalent` | same program, comments differ | |
| `utils/generators/hlsPlaylistGenerator` | same program, quote style differs | |
| `utils/parsers/parseFullName` | same program, comments and one pair of parentheses differ | |
| `utils/parsers/parseUserAgent` | same program, quote style differs | |
| `utils/parsers/parseNfoMetadata` | same statements, one reordered | `module.exports` is now assigned after a hoisted helper function; `BookFinder.ts` already compiles this way |
| `providers/OpenLibrary` | same program, one statement split in two | the `axios` import, same shape as `AuthorFinder.ts`; `BookFinder.ts` compiles unchanged |

There is no `any` and no `@ts-ignore` in the 14 files. Where the compiler needed help I used type-only assertions, each with a comment saying why.

One departure from the finders' style: `Notification.ts` and `Task.ts` keep a plain `require('uuid')` with a type annotation, because `uuid` has no type declarations and `import uuid = require('uuid')` does not compile.

## How I checked behaviour is unchanged

- **Whole build:** a from-scratch build produces the same 463 files; 454 are byte-identical to the original build, and the 9 that differ are all in the table above.
- **Side-by-side execution:** I ran the old and new compiled modules on 4,705 identical inputs and every result matched. I confirmed the harness detects a deliberately planted change in each of the 14 modules.
- **Running server:** I booted the old and new builds in a scratch directory and ran the same API script against each. The script covered login, the notification lifecycle, a library scan of a tagged MP3 plus `.nfo`, an HLS session and a share with a 40-day expiry. All 27 comparable steps matched on every run.

The verification scripts are in the session scratchpad, not in the repository.

## What I could not verify

- **OpenLibrary against the live service, fully.** Title search returned identical data from both builds. The ISBN lookup comparison was inconclusive: it differed once, and the site stopped answering before I could confirm why. Against a local stand-in server both builds made the same requests and returned the same results.
- **`TrackProgressMonitor` in a running server.** That needs an m4b encode job; it is covered by its unit tests and the side-by-side runs only.
- **`stringifySequelizeQuery` in a running server.** The item listing I called should go through it, but I did not observe it directly.
- **Linux, Docker and the packaged binary.** I only ran on Windows with Node 24. The compiled files have the same names and paths as before, so the `pkg` globs should match the same files, but I did not run that workflow.

If you repeat the HLS step on Windows you may see `Ffmpeg Err "ffmpeg exited with code 143"` in the log. The original build logs it too (4 of 5 runs), so it is not from this change.

## For you to decide (I changed none of these)

- **`uuid` is not in `package.json`.** It is installed only because `sequelize` depends on it, yet 18 server files require it. Adding `uuid` and `@types/uuid` would let the two plain `require` lines use the normal import form.
- **ESLint skips every `.ts` file**, including the existing finders, so `npm run lint` passing says nothing about them. Linting them would need a TypeScript parser in the ESLint config.
- **`server/finders/BookFinder.ts` has stale comments** (out of scope). Lines 39 and 51 cite `OpenLibrary.js:46, :85` and `:35, :114`; those are now `OpenLibrary.ts:109, :148` and `:98, :177`.
- **The tests need no changes.**

## Existing quirks this surfaced (left as they were)

- **`OpenLibrary.isbnLookup`** requests a URL without `.json`, so it returns the book's HTML page as a string, not JSON. Its only caller, `BookFinder.findByISBN`, is unused. I typed it to say so; `BookFinder.ts` still describes it as JSON.
- **`areEquivalent`** throws "value1 is circular" when the same array instance appears twice in the first value. It also contains a `'function'` check that can never be true.
- **`parseFullName`** compares `fixCase` with the string `'undefined'`, which is always unequal.
- **Notification templates** treat `$` sequences in event data specially: a podcast titled `Cash $$ Flow` is sent as `Cash $ Flow`.
- **`AudioMetaTags.isEqual`** only checks the tags present on the other object, so a tag removed from a file still compares as equal.
- **`Task.failedAt`** is set on failure but never included in `toJSON()`.
- **`TaskManager`** passes `null` as task data in one place; `Task.setData` now declares that it accepts it.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **`declare` on class fields matters here.** With this project's ES2022 target, an ordinary field declaration compiles to a real field. `AudioMetaTags.toJSON()` walks the instance with `for…in`, so that could have changed which keys appear and in what order; `declare` emits nothing.
- **`export =` always lands at the end of the compiled file.** That was harmless for `parseNfoMetadata`, but in a file with side effects after its export, or one in a circular `require`, it could change behaviour. Worth checking on future conversions.
- **Comparing compiled output is a cheap proof for a types-only migration.** The server runs from `dist-server/`, so if a `.ts` file compiles to the same JavaScript as its `.js` predecessor, behaviour cannot have changed.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

4	// lib.d.ts types isNaN(number), but the built-in coerces every value and parsePublishYear() calls it with the year part of a date string. Widens the type for this file only; emits no code.
5	declare function isNaN(value: unknown): boolean
6	
7	// The three interfaces below describe OpenLibrary's JSON, limited to the fields that are read here. It is external data: the server does not validate it.
8	
9	/** A doc in a search.json response */
10	interface OpenLibrarySearchDoc {
11	  key: string
12	  title: string
13	  author_name?: string[]
14	  first_publish_year?: number
15	  cover_edition_key?: string
16	}
17	
18	interface OpenLibrarySearchResponse {
19	  docs: OpenLibrarySearchDoc[]
20	}
21	
22	/** A works record (<works key>.json) */
23	interface OpenLibraryWorksResponse {
24	  covers?: number[]
25	  description?: string | { value?: string }
26	  first_publish_date?: string
27	}
28	
29	/** Returned in place of data when a request to OpenLibrary fails */
30	interface OpenLibraryRequestError {
31	  errorCode: 404
32	}
33	
34	/** Returned by getWorksData() when the works request fails. cleanSearchDoc() spreads it into the search hit just like a successful result. */
35	interface OpenLibraryWorksError {
36	  errorMsg: string
37	  errorCode: 500
38	  first_publish_date?: undefined // read by parsePublishYear() without checking for the error first
39	}
40	
41	interface OpenLibraryWorksData {
42	  /** Last segment of the works key. split() never returns an empty array, hence the non-null assertion in getWorksData(). */
43	  id: string
44	  key: string
45	  covers: string[]
46	  first_publish_date: string | undefined
47	  description: string | null
48	}
49	
50	/** A search hit: fields from the search doc, with the works data (or the works error) spread over them */
51	type OpenLibrarySearchResult = {
52	  title: string
53	  author: string | null
54	  publishedYear: string | null
55	  edition: string | undefined
56	  cover: string | null
57	} & (OpenLibraryWorksData | OpenLibraryWorksError)
58	
59	class OpenLibrary {
60	  #responseTimeout = 10000
61	
62	  declare baseUrl: string
63	
64	  constructor() {
65	    this.baseUrl = 'https://openlibrary.org'
66	  }
67	
68	  /**
69	   *
70	   * @template T the shape the caller expects back; the response is not checked against it
71	   * @param {string} uri
72	   * @param {number} timeout
73	   * @returns {Promise<Object>}
74	   */
75	  get<T>(uri: string, timeout: number = this.#responseTimeout): Promise<T | null> {
76	    if (!timeout || isNaN(timeout)) timeout = this.#responseTimeout
77	    return axios
78	      .get<T>(`${this.baseUrl}/${uri}`, {
79	        timeout
80	      })
81	      .then((res) => {
82	        return res.data
83	      })
84	      .catch((error) => {
85	        console.error('Failed', error.message)
86	        return null
87	      })
88	  }
89	
90	  /**
91	   * The URL has no ".json" suffix, and OpenLibrary answers it with the book's HTML page, so in practice this resolves to that page as a string rather than to a JSON record.
92	   * Left as it was, since changing the URL would change behaviour. Its only caller is BookFinder.findByISBN(), which nothing calls at the time of writing.
93	   */
94	  async isbnLookup(isbn: string): Promise<Record<string, unknown> | string | OpenLibraryRequestError> {
95	    var lookupData = await this.get<Record<string, unknown> | string>(`/isbn/${isbn}`)
96	    if (!lookupData) {
97	      return {
98	        errorCode: 404
99	      }
100	    }
101	    return lookupData
102	  }
103	
104	  async getWorksData(worksKey: string): Promise<OpenLibraryWorksData | OpenLibraryWorksError> {
105	    var worksData = await this.get<OpenLibraryWorksResponse>(`${worksKey}.json`)
106	    if (!worksData) {
107	      return {
108	        errorMsg: 'Works Data Request failed',
109	        errorCode: 500
110	      }
111	    }
112	    if (!worksData.covers) worksData.covers = []
113	    var coverImages = worksData.covers.filter((c) => c > 0).map((c) => `https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/id/${c}-L.jpg`)
114	    var description: string | null = null
115	    if (worksData.description) {
116	      if (typeof worksData.description === 'string') {
117	        description = worksData.description
118	      } else {
119	        description = worksData.description.value || null
120	      }
121	    }
122	    return {
123	      id: worksKey.split('/').pop()!,
124	      key: worksKey,
125	      covers: coverImages,
126	      first_publish_date: worksData.first_publish_date,
127	      description: description
128	    }
129	  }
130	
131	  parsePublishYear(doc: OpenLibrarySearchDoc, worksData: OpenLibraryWorksData | OpenLibraryWorksError): string | null {
132	    if (doc.first_publish_year && !isNaN(doc.first_publish_year)) return String(doc.first_publish_year)
133	    if (worksData.first_publish_date) {
134	      var year = worksData.first_publish_date.split('-')[0]
135	      if (!isNaN(year)) return String(year)
136	    }
137	    return null
138	  }
139	
140	  async cleanSearchDoc(doc: OpenLibrarySearchDoc): Promise<OpenLibrarySearchResult> {
141	    var worksData = await this.getWorksData(doc.key)
142	    return {
143	      title: doc.title,
144	      author: doc.author_name ? doc.author_name.join(', ') : null,
145	      publishedYear: this.parsePublishYear(doc, worksData),
146	      edition: doc.cover_edition_key,
147	      cover: doc.cover_edition_key ? `https://covers.openlibrary.org/b/OLID/${doc.cover_edition_key}-L.jpg` : null,
148	      ...worksData
149	    }
150	  }
151	
152	  async search(query: Record<string, string | number | boolean>): Promise<OpenLibrarySearchResult[] | OpenLibraryRequestError> {
153	    var queryString = Object.keys(query)
154	      .map((key) => key + '=' + query[key])
155	      .join('&')
156	    var lookupData = await this.get<OpenLibrarySearchResponse>(`/search.json?${queryString}`)
157	    if (!lookupData) {
158	      return {
159	        errorCode: 404
160	      }
161	    }
162	    var searchDocs = await Promise.all(lookupData.docs.map((d) => this.cleanSearchDoc(d)))
163	    return searchDocs
164	  }
165	
166	  /**
167	   *
168	   * @param {string} title
169	   * @param {number} timeout
170	   * @returns {Promise<Object[]>}
171	   */
172	  async searchTitle(title: string, timeout: number = this.#responseTimeout): Promise<OpenLibrarySearchResult[] | OpenLibraryRequestError> {
173	    title = encodeURIComponent(title)
174	    var lookupData = await this.get<OpenLibrarySearchResponse>(`/search.json?title=${title}`, timeout)
175	    if (!lookupData) {
176	      return {
177	        errorCode: 404
178	      }
179	    }
180	    var searchDocs = await Promise.all(lookupData.docs.map((d) => this.cleanSearchDoc(d)))
181	    return searchDocs
182	  }
183	}
184	export = OpenLibrary
185

#!/bin/bash
# Boots one compiled server tree in an isolated scratch directory, runs smoke.js against it, then stops it.
# Usage: runsmoke.sh <label> <path to compiled index.js> <port> <cwd for the server> [NODE_PATH]
# Nothing outside the scratchpad is written: config, metadata and the library all live under e2e/<label>.
SP="/c/Users/USER/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/D--SEM-2-574-po-s06-run-audiobookshelf/44babef5-5841-4659-9823-eee1f53febf0/scratchpad"
LABEL="$1"; INDEX="$2"; PORT="$3"; SERVER_CWD="$4"; NP="$5"
if [ -z "$LABEL" ] || [ -z "$INDEX" ] || [ -z "$PORT" ] || [ -z "$SERVER_CWD" ]; then echo "usage error"; exit 2; fi

RUN="$SP/e2e/$LABEL"
case "$RUN" in "$SP"/e2e/?*) ;; *) echo "refusing to use run dir $RUN"; exit 2 ;; esac
rm -rf "$RUN"
mkdir -p "$RUN/lib"
cp -r "$SP/smoke-src/." "$RUN/lib/"
RUNW="$(cygpath -m "$RUN")"

FFMPEG="$(cygpath -m "$(which ffmpeg)")"
FFPROBE="$(cygpath -m "$(which ffprobe)")"
case "$FFMPEG" in *.exe) ;; *) FFMPEG="$FFMPEG.exe" ;; esac
case "$FFPROBE" in *.exe) ;; *) FFPROBE="$FFPROBE.exe" ;; esac
[ -f "$FFMPEG" ] && [ -f "$FFPROBE" ] || { echo "ffmpeg/ffprobe not found"; exit 2; }

(
  cd "$SERVER_CWD" || exit 2
  # SKIP_BINARIES_CHECK stops the server from downloading ffmpeg; the two paths point at the copies already installed
  FFMPEG_PATH="$FFMPEG" FFPROBE_PATH="$FFPROBE" SKIP_BINARIES_CHECK=1 NODE_PATH="$NP" \
    node "$INDEX" --config "$RUNW/config" --metadata "$RUNW/metadata" --port "$PORT" --host 127.0.0.1 --source smoke > "$RUN/server.log" 2>&1 &
  echo $! > "$RUN/pid"
)
PID="$(cat "$RUN/pid")"

UP=0
for i in $(seq 1 80); do
  if curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/audiobookshelf/ping" > /dev/null 2>&1; then UP=1; break; fi
  if ! kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 0.5
done
if [ "$UP" != 1 ]; then
  echo "[$LABEL] SERVER DID NOT COME UP"; tail -30 "$RUN/server.log"; kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 1
fi
echo "[$LABEL] server is up on 127.0.0.1:$PORT (pid $PID)"

node "$(cygpath -m "$SP/smoke.js")" "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/audiobookshelf" "$RUNW/lib" "$RUNW/transcript.json"
SMOKE_EXIT=$?

kill "$PID" 2>/dev/null
for i in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.25; done
kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null
echo "[$LABEL] server stopped; smoke exit=$SMOKE_EXIT"
echo "[$LABEL] error/fatal lines in server log: $(grep -c -i -E "\b(ERROR|FATAL)\b" "$RUN/server.log")"
exit $SMOKE_EXIT

5	// Usage: node astdiff.js <repo root> <baseline dist dir> <relative path without extension> [...]
6	const fs = require('fs')

12	function parse(file) {

14	  const comments = []
15	  const ast = acorn.parse(src, { ecmaVersion: 'latest', sourceType: 'script', allowHashBang: true, onComment: comments })
16	  return { ast, src, comments }
17	}

19	// Drop position info. Literal.raw is dropped too (quote style / numeric spelling), but the cooked `value`,
20	// `regex` and `bigint` fields are kept, and TemplateElement.value.raw is kept.
21	function clean(node, parentType) {
22	  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.map((n) => clean(n, parentType))
23	  if (node && typeof node === 'object') {
24	    if (node instanceof RegExp) return { __regexp: String(node) }
25	    const out = {}
26	    for (const key of Object.keys(node)) {
27	      if (key === 'start' || key === 'end' || key === 'loc' || key === 'range') continue
28	      if (key === 'raw' && node.type === 'Literal') continue
29	      const v = node[key]
30	      out[key] = typeof v === 'bigint' ? { __bigint: String(v) } : clean(v, node.type)
31	    }
32	    return out
33	  }
34	  return node
35	}
36	
37	function firstDifference(a, b, trail) {
38	  if (a === b) return null
39	  if (typeof a !== typeof b || a === null || b === null || typeof a !== 'object') return `${trail}: ${JSON.stringify(a)} !== ${JSON.stringify(b)}`
40	  if (Array.isArray(a) !== Array.isArray(b)) return `${trail}: array/object mismatch`
41	  const keys = new Set([...Object.keys(a), ...Object.keys(b)])
42	  for (const key of keys) {
43	    if (!(key in a) || !(key in b)) return `${trail}.${key}: present on one side only`
44	    const d = firstDifference(a[key], b[key], `${trail}.${key}`)
45	    if (d) return d
46	  }
47	  return null
48	}

50	// JavaScript instantiates every top-level function declaration before the first statement of the file runs, so where a
51	// function declaration sits relative to the other statements cannot affect execution. Model that by moving them to the
52	// front, keeping the relative order of the declarations and of the remaining statements (tsc emits `export =` last).
53	function hoistFunctionDeclarations(program) {
54	  const fns = program.body.filter((n) => n.type === 'FunctionDeclaration')
55	  const rest = program.body.filter((n) => n.type !== 'FunctionDeclaration')

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:
